Below the text a Greek verse line and a Latin verse quotation are set in the body. Running head at top, page number at top left, catchword "Spe-" at lower right.

main_text.p: Tiberius.rem. & huic ipsi Tiberio: quem genere adoptionis filium, collegam imperii, confortem tribunitiae potestatis po-teftatis, non ad extremum dilexit. Unde ea potentia in aula, unde gratiae mutatio? Invenerit aliquid Au-gustus offensione in Tiberio dignum, tetricam nimirum morum arrogantiam: offenderit cum Agrippae cum Marcello simultas: cum Graecorum proverbio, Mutationisμία λόγῳ δύο ἐξ ἰσότητος [?] Non tulerit civilia Marcelli & Drusi ingenia, populique in utrumque ocu-los converfos. Caufam mobilis potentiae generalio-rem, & omnibus ubique adaptandam, Cornelius ex-primit: Fato potentia raro fempiternae. nam quae ab opum diftributione adjunguntur, an fatis capit, autem illos cum omnia tribuerunt, aut hos, cum jam nihil re-liquum eft quod cupiant, nimis pro rerum amplitudine ne funt anguftae. Alios aetas, & cum aetate mores im-mutant: alios irrepentium adulatorum fufurratio: alios facti alicujus occulta exprobratio. fic quia Te-rentiam Maecenatis uxorem Augustus adulterio co-gnovit, eamque rem aegre Maecenas tulit, multum de gratia imminutum, quia Poppaeam folus ductare Ne-ro defideravit, Orbonem ab aula removit. Haec in praecepta ac in ordinem cogere idem effet, ac fi quis ipfas hominum cupiditates, modi ac fpatii refcias, & mobiles omnium voluntates, lege & modo circum-feribat.
Phylaëte-tis.In qua cupidinum humanarum infinitate, cautio-num monita finita aut facilia dari non poffunt. E mul-tis tamen pauca, in aulicorum ufum, delibabo.
J.1. Nunquam ita blandienti ferenitati credas, ut non in irruentes imbres penulam paratam geras. fic fiet, ut aut depellas pluviam moleftiam, aut praevifam aequi animo feras.
3.2. Diffidentis animi indicia abfcondas; monitu Euripidis:

page.notes: Top of the page is a partly legible running head; the number "210" is uncertain. Greek lines are not fully legible and are marked [?]; the Greek verse after Euripidis was read only in part. Left margin notes are placed by their position beside the text lines. The Latin verse "Nam fronte cauta tecta diffidentia" and "Immane quanto commodo gentes juvat" are copied as printed and not checked against the source. Several words in the Latin body are uncertain and may contain errors; the page is a dense scan and some words could not be confirmed letter by letter. The "3. Spe-" line at the foot is taken as a catchword in the bottom margin and as a note of the same text, and may need to be checked.
